text_devanagari: अच्छा॑ म॒ इन्द्रं॑ म॒तयः॑ स्व॒र्विदः॑ स॒ध्रीची॒र्विश्वा॑ उश॒तीर॑नूषत । ॥ १७ ॥
y_bands: Measured on the deskewed line (a shear of 0.00616 px/px removes the ~20 px page skew across the 3226 px line; raw block-y of any mark = deskewed y + round(0.00616 * x_global)). Bands in deskewed block-y: line-above (line 8) anudatta bar band 1662-1695, then a dead-white gutter 1696-1876 (zero inked pixels across the full 3226 px width, apart from one 3x4 px speck at x3049, y1758-1761); MY svarita band, clear above the sirorekha, 1877-1911; MY sirorekha 1912-1930 (row-ink plateau 2200-2270 px at rows 1917-1929); MY glyph body 1931-1994; MY descender zone (u/uu matras, subscript-ra wedges, terminal flicks) 1995-2020; MY OWN anudatta bar band 2021-2033 (peak row-ink 269 at row 2026), then white 2034-2052; the next line's (line 10) svarita band 2053-2092; line 10 sirorekha 2093-2112; line 10's own bar band 2196-2208. Line pitch is 175 px: line 10's sirorekha and bar band each sit exactly 175 px below mine. Line 8's bar band is TWO pitches above mine, not one, because there is extra leading (a hymn break) between line 8 and line 9 - hence the 181-row band of pure white above my svarita band. That is the control that makes line attribution unambiguous here: nothing from the line above can reach either of my bands. In raw (skewed) block-y the six bars run y2027-2036 at x506 and y2036-2048 at x2211.
boundary_interpretation: Word boundaries came from the column ink profile of the body band ONLY (deskewed y1934-1993, i.e. below the sirorekha and above the descenders), so the headline could not bridge glyphs. Gaps inside a word are 8-23 px; gaps between words are 50-59 px - a clean bimodal split with nothing in between, so none of the seven word breaks is a judgement call. Body-band runs (|| = word break, | = aksara-element break): 184-282 | 284-362 | 375-395 || 453-525 || 578-628 | 637-717 || 768-840 | 854-908 | 924-982 | 1006-1027 || 1087-1203 | 1215-1232 | 1255-1310 | 1324-1376 | 1398-1419 || 1472-1542 | 1555-1615 | 1630-1650 | 1668-1735 | 1755-1772 | 1794-1811 | 1835-1892 | 1907-1983 | 2003-2021 || 2078-2144 | 2155-2226 | 2238-2291 | 2310-2329 | 2345-2452 | 2467-2520 | 2535-2589 || 2649-2666 (danda) || 2932-2953, 2956-2974 (double danda) || 2998-3048, 3058-3122 (verse numerals) || 3146-3184 (final double danda: two strokes, 3146-3161 and 3164-3184, that touch at a single column). Aksara indices count graphic clusters, with matra, visarga and a preceding repha folded into the cluster they are drawn on: accha = [a][cchaa]; ma = [ma]; indram = [i][ndram]; matayah = [ma][ta][yah]; svarvidah = [sva][rvi][dah]; sadhriiciirvishvaa = [sa][dhrii][cii][rvi][shvaa]; ushatiiranuushata = [u][sha][tii][ra][nuu][sha][ta]. Marks near a boundary, and how each was decided. All six bars lie wholly inside one body-band run, and this print sets a bar under the RIGHT part of its aksara with the bar's right edge flush to the aksara's right edge - a rule that held for all six without exception. (1) x820 in matayah: bar spans 801-839, ma spans 768-840, ta starts at 854. The centre is 34 px inside ma, the right edge 1 px inside ma's, and the bar does not overlap ta at all -> ma, not ta. The isolated one-letter word ma at 453-525 carries its bar at 488-525, the same 72-79% offset, which is what establishes the rule. (2) x1525 in sadhriiciirvishvaa: bar 1507-1543, sa 1472-1542, next element starts 1555; right edge 1 px past sa's, still 12 px clear of the next -> sa. (3) x2211 in ushatiiranuushata: bar 2192-2230, sha 2155-2226, ta starts 2238; right edge 4 px past sha's, 8 px clear of ta -> sha. (4) x1716: bar 1697-1734 under ca 1668-1735; the preceding cluster dhrii ends at 1650 and 1651-1667 is empty -> cii, not dhrii. (5) x1173: falls under the subscript va of the sva conjunct (single run 1087-1203), one aksara, so index 0 either way. All six svaritas fall wholly within a single body-band run's x-span - four of them right-of-centre over it, two effectively centred - and none is within 10 px of a run boundary, so no svarita required a side decision. The only orthographic (not spatial) call is the repha in -rvi-: ra+virama is drawn above the headline, and I count it with the following vi as the graphic cluster [rvi], which is why svarvidah has 3 aksaras and not 4. No accent mark sits on a repha, so this choice moves no carrier.
notes: Method. I worked from the source scan, not from the supplied crops alone: leaf bsb10219750_00411.jpg, text block (412,382)-(3638,5388) = 3226x5006, line 9 at block y1890-2011. Global line-x equals block-x (seg1_x/0.9440 inverts to block-x exactly), so every x reported is directly comparable. Measurement was by PIL row and column ink profiles and 8-connected component extents at thresholds 140, 170 and 190, plus my own crops rendered at 2.4x-15.7x of the native raster (the 4000 px file is an upscale of a 2024 px master, so this is magnification, not extra detail). I deskewed by a 0.00616 px/px shear before banding; that sharpened the sirorekha and put all six bars at one identical deskewed y-centre of 2028.4 - independent confirmation that they are one line's bar row and not a mixture of two lines'. ANUDATTA: 6 found, every one isolated and inside my own bar band, 37-39 px wide by 10-13 px tall (aspect 3.0-3.8), centres x507, 820, 1173, 1525, 1716, 2211. The row-ink budget agrees: peak 269 px in the bar band minus the ~50 px descender floor leaves ~219 px, i.e. six bars of ~38 px with no room for a seventh. SVARITA: 6 found, isolated upright strokes standing clear above the sirorekha, 11-17 px wide by >=29 px tall (aspect 0.38-0.50), centres x327, 694, 963, 1357, 1970, 2366. Rejected false positives, by shape. (a) Six wide curved shapes above the headline: x1216-1301 (86 px, repha plus i-matra of -rvi- in svarvidah, two merged hooks), x1590-1646 (57 px, ii-matra of dhrii), x1714-1773 (60 px, ii-matra of cii), x1795-1841 (47 px, repha) and x1843-1887 (45 px, i-matra of vi) in -rvishvaa, x2270-2327 (58 px, ii-matra of tii). All are hooks or crescents in the 50-68 px matra class, or two such merged, not narrow uprights. (b) One round dot, x703-720 in indram, about 16x16 and sitting lower than its neighbour: anusvara, not svarita. The stroke beside it at x686-702 IS a svarita; the two are separate blobs that only merge at threshold 140, and the stroke tops out 13 rows higher. (c) In the bar band, component x2412-2480 (deskewed y2014-2031, aspect 1.5-2.1) is the uu-matra of nuu in ushatiiranuushata: a curved hook running continuously up into the body with no white gap, so not a bar. (d) Thin diagonal terminal flicks under cha, i, sa, sha and da (attached, diagonal, 25-35 px long, in the descender zone y1995-2020) - the halanta-tail class; none is a horizontal dash and none reaches the bar band. (e) A 3x4 px speck at x3049, y1758-1761 in the empty gutter: noise, far too small for either mark. (f) Nothing accentual right of x2366 - the danda at 2649-2666, the double dandas and the numerals carry nothing above or below them. Unresolved. One cluster, the second aksara of word 5 (body-band run 1555-1615 plus its subscript wedge): I read it as dha + subscript ra = dhrii, but at this raster I cannot fully exclude shri, so I have counted it in unclear_count. It carries no accent mark, so it cannot move any carrier. A lesser doubt I did not count: the second verse numeral (x3058-3122) is a bold loop with a tail curling to the bottom-left, which I read as 7, giving 17; it is clearly not a 9 (no straight right descender) and not a 0. For the record, word 1 is a bare single letter ma carrying an anudatta - unusual as a word, but the ink shows one glyph at 453-525 with nothing above the headline and no matra, so that is what I recorded rather than smoothing it to me or maa. The first glyph of the line was read as a per the fount note; it does look like vocalic r to a modern eye.
